sections.content: How many people are "floorers and wall tilers"?

45,415 people

were counted on the census as "floorers and wall tilers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Floorers and wall tilers lay composition mixtures (other than mastic asphalt) to form flooring, plan, fit and secure carpet, underlay and linoleum and cover and decorate walls and floors with terrazzo and granolithic mixtures, tiles and mosaic panels.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "floorers and wall tilers" there were more men than women (98.1% compared with 1.9%).

This means "floorers and wall tilers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled construction and building trades".

Men made up 98.1% and women made up 1.9% of "floorers and wall tilers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "floorers and wall tilers" included:

  • large goods vehicle drivers
  • mobile machine drivers and operatives (other)
  • vehicle technicians, mechanics and electricians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "floorers and wall tilers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "floorers and wall tilers", 13.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "floorers and wall tilers" was 16 to 19 years.

  • bakers and flour confectioners
  • glaziers, window fabricators and fitters
  • vehicle paint technicians

We can look at who worked as "floorers and wall tilers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "floorers and wall tilers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "floorers and wall tilers", 7.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (75.1% compared with 24.9%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (74.4%) than an employee (25.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
